confirmed.summary: `bg_color white` runs without error but the live WebGL viewport never repaints — background stays black.
confirmed.repro: 1) Load scene, `as cartoon`. 2) Run `bg_color white`. 3) Observe interactive viewport: backdrop remains black instead of turning white (command echoed, no error). Independently reproduced via scripts/audit/run-shard.mjs on /tmp/verify-viewport_render_bgColor.json → FAIL "viewport unchanged".
confirmed.evidence: Fresh screenshot /tmp/vshots/viewport.render.bgColor.png shows black background after `bg_color white` (console shows the command, no console/page errors). Root cause: viewport renderer has setBackground (packages/viewport/src/modeG/renderer.ts:178-181,292-294; viewport.ts:854-855) but the web app never wires the bg_rgb setting to it — background is only ever initialized to null (viewport.ts:195); no bg_rgb→setBackground subscription exists in apps/web/src. Ray path honors bg_rgb (engine-ts/src/cmd/render.ts:42-48,95), so only the interactive canvas is affected.

confirmed.summary: Frame scrollbar (range input) stays permanently disabled on the local engine because get_movie_status is a stub that always reports nframes:0, even after mset defines a movie.
confirmed.evidence: Independent reproduction via the audit harness (?backend=local). After setup `mset 1 x30`: cmd.count_frames=30 and cmd.get_movie_length=30 (movie genuinely created), but cmd.get_movie_status returned {frame:1,nframes:0,...}. Panel showed "FRAME 1/0 · no movie — define one with mset below" and the range element was <input min=1 max=1 disabled value=1>, so Playwright locator.fill times out. Root cause: packages/engine-ts/src/engine.ts:986 registers get_movie_status as a fixed stub returning nframes:0; registerSystem in packages/engine-ts/src/cmd/system.ts overrides get_frame/count_frames/get_movie_length but NOT get_movie_status. apps/web/src/features/movie/movieSource.ts status() calls cmd.get_movie_status first (ensure() succeeds since the stub does not throw) and only falls back to count_frames if it throws, so MoviePanel.tsx:179 keeps the range disabled (nframes<1) forever. The disabled state is the real bug, not a check/timing artifact.
confirmed.repro: 1) Open the app with ?backend=local. 2) In the movie panel run `mset 1 x30` to define a 30-frame movie. 3) Observe the readout still says "FRAME 1/0 · no movie" and the .mvpanel__range input remains disabled (max=1), so the frame scrollbar cannot be moved. Engine-internally cmd.count_frames returns 30 but cmd.get_movie_status still returns nframes:0.

confirmed.summary: Scene menu ▸ Blank fails to clear the viewport — it throws "CmdException: No scenes" and leaves the molecule fully rendered instead of disabling all objects.
confirmed.repro: 1. Load default session (backend tenmol-engine-ts). 2. Open the Scene panel; click the "Blank" button (.scmenu .scmenu__row button, nth 12), which runs cmd.scene("", "recall"). 3. Observe: the molecule stays fully rendered (viewport unchanged) and the output log shows red "CmdException: No scenes". Expected: screen goes blank (all objects disabled, message cleared).
confirmed.evidence: Fresh shard run (/tmp/verify-scmenu_blank.out.json) → FAIL screenshotChanged "viewport unchanged". Fresh screenshot /tmp/vshots/scmenu.blank.png: cartoon still fully rendered; output panel shows cmd.scene("", "recall") followed by "CmdException: No scenes"; SCENES 0, current: (none). This is not a check/timing artifact — the control genuinely errored and did nothing. Frontend maps Blank → sceneActions.blank() = scene(['','recall']) (apps/web/src/features/scenes/sceneActions.ts:82; SceneMenu.tsx:70), whose own comment says recall '' should "disable all + clear the message". Reference PyMOL engine MovieScene.cpp:794-806 handles empty-key recall via ExecutiveSetObjVisib(G,"*",false,false) (blank screen) and only raises "No scenes" (MovieScene.cpp:783,839) for next/previous/start — so the engine-ts backend wrongly hits the No-scenes path for empty-key recall. Note: the prior audit screenshot (21 scenes) also showed the viewport not blanking, so the affordance is broken regardless of scene count.

confirmed.summary: Clicking the "Builder" quick button opens the panel slot but the Builder dock window fails to render on cold load, so the Triple-bond control is unreachable.
confirmed.repro: One-spec shard at /tmp/verify-builder_bonds_order_triple.json fails 3/3: "TimeoutError: page.waitForSelector: Timeout 6000ms exceeded — waiting for [data-testid=builder-window]", at the setup step (before builder_dismiss), with zero console/page errors — refuting the reported Clear-modal cascade. Root cause: apps/web/src/shell/FeatureSlot.tsx mounts <MountMarker> before <Panel/> in the same Suspense; MountMarker's useEffect calls panelMounted() (apps/web/src/shell/panelHooks.ts) and dispatches tenmol:open-builder before BuilderPanel's addEventListener runs (apps/web/src/features/builder/BuilderPanel.tsx:112-114), so the open-intent is lost.
confirmed.evidence: Deterministic audit FAIL (3 runs) in isolation with no Clear modal; live-browser confirmation that the panel mounts but never opens until the open event is re-dispatched; effect-ordering race in FeatureSlot.tsx / panelHooks.ts / BuilderPanel.tsx:112-114.

confirmed.summary: The "Builder" quick button deterministically fails to open the Builder dock on the first click (mount-vs-listener race), so Model ▸ Sculpt is unreachable via that affordance on first attempt.
confirmed.repro: 1) Fresh app at /?backend=local. 2) Click the quick button `.quickbuttons button[title='the builder dock']` exactly once. 3) Observe: no `[data-testid=builder-window]` / `.flwin` appears within 6s+ (audit setup times out here). confirmed.evidence: Not a "Clear modal cascade" — reproduced in full isolation with a one-spec shard (FAIL 3/3 runs, all "waitForSelector builder-window Timeout 6000ms"; no console errors, no pageerrors, no netFailures). Instrumented the isolated driver: after one click, `document.body.dataset.features` DOES gain "builder" (slot mounts) but `builderWin=false, flwin=0`; dispatching `tenmol:open-builder` manually then opens it (`flwin=1`). Root cause in apps/web: QuickButtons.tsx:180-183 `openBuilder` calls `openPanel('builder', () => dispatchEvent(OPEN_EVENT))`; panelHooks.ts:109-116 `panelMounted` drains that intent from FeatureSlot.tsx's `MountMarker` useEffect, which commits BEFORE the sibling BuilderPanel's own `addEventListener(OPEN_EVENT)` useEffect (BuilderPanel.tsx:111-115) — so the first OPEN_EVENT is dispatched before any listener exists and is lost. On the 2nd click the slot is already mounted so the intent runs synchronously with the listener present → opens. Confirmed by /tmp/debug-builder3.mjs: 1st click {win:false}, 2nd click {win:true, bbtn:56, sculpt:true}. Net user impact: clicking Builder once appears to do nothing (only a secondary "builder-launch" button surfaces); this race blocks the one-click open of the entire Builder dock and thus every builder.* spec's setup. Sculpt itself is fine once the dock is open, so the defect is the shared first-click dock-open race, not the Sculpt control.
